Values and Ethos
Vision
At Rockmount Primary School we will inspire our whole school community to enjoy their learning adventure and have fun along the way. We will ignite a passion for learning throughout the school community, securing excellence, empathy and equality in all that we do, with emotional wellbeing and mental health at the heart of our aspirations.
Mission
We will strive to achieve the highest standards of academic achievement and behaviour within an inclusive, vibrant and exciting learning environment to ensure that all children leave school with the confidence and ability to take full advantage of future opportunities.
School Values
Our school ethos is underpinned by our Rockmount School Values. Each of these values has been identified as key to the children developing emotional intelligence and being successful learners.
Promoting British Values
Our school values deliberately embrace those fundamental values which run through every element of school life and life outside of school.
British values are promoted in much of what we do, during school assemblies, circle times, Religious Education and PSHE sessions. They are integral to both our vision and values and can be seen across the school; helping to support our children for life in Modern Britain. We recognise that these values are not unique to Britain. We acknowledge that they differ in no way from the values of the many countries and the cultural backgrounds represented by families at Rockmount. We understand and celebrate the diversity within our society and school community and ensure that British Values are embedded within our curriculum when Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural (SMSC) learning takes place across all curriculum areas.
Fundamental British values are defined as:
We promote British Values in the following ways (please note that this list is not exhaustive):
Democracy
Individual liberty
The rule of law
Mutual respect and tolerance
Bi-annual parent questionnaires.
Governor involvement in decision making process.
Agreement of Class Rules annually.
Home/School Agreement
Open and honest culture.
Visits arranged to different places of worship.

Welcome
Welcome to Rockmount Primary School
Rockmount is a happy, friendly school situated very close to the vibrant Crystal Palace triangle. We greatly value our very strong and diverse school community and work hard to ensure good relationships are built on support, kindness and consideration for all.
From the first day a child attends, our priority is to provide a safe, caring and stimulating environment for them to learn and grow. We seek to provide aspirational and creative opportunities for them to discover their individual potential and to excel. Pupils are encouraged to explore their own interests to support them in the development of high self-esteem and a passion for continuous learning.
Rockmount provides a strong academic platform for pupils within a school ethos which is firmly embedded in wellbeing for all. Our partnership with families is essential in helping to build a clear picture of every child as an individual and in helping to shape the future development of the school. We actively encourage a close partnership between home and school so that parents and carers can be involved in their child’s education and in school life. Everyone is appreciated for their contribution to the school community and is supported to make their way towards a purposeful and fulfilled life as we move forward in an ever-changing world.
With high expectations, we are committed to fulfilling our motto, "All Can Achieve". This is the central premise of all that happens in our school.
This website provides a wealth of information about how Rockmount is organised and a window into the memorable learning experiences our children enjoy. Of course, our school is much more than the website can show and we encourage you to visit us to see Rockmount for yourself; you will be made very welcome.

Rockmount Children's Club
Our Extended School Day provision is available from Reception to Year 6 and offers a safe environment, varied timetable of activities and healthy meals. The service is run by school staff and led by Ana de Miguel, our Extended Services Manager. We currently have some availability for Reception children.
We cannot cater for Nursery pupils at Rockmount After School Club.
Please find the RCC Transition Booklet below:
Transition Booklet Breakfast and Afterschool Club
Have a look at our brochure
When printed it will be in the form of a booklet.
Please note that the After School Club is closed on the last day of each term.
Please note that late collection of children will result in a late collection fee, payable on Parent Pay. (See Policy)
The breakfast and after school clubs provide activities and healthy meals for pupils at Rockmount School from Reception to Year 6. To find out more please contact extendedschools@rockmount.croydon.sch.uk or telephone (020) 8683 8451.
Staff at both clubs are fully qualified and also employed in other roles at the school, so they are familiar to the children and very much part of the school community. This means class teachers can make breakfast/after school club staff aware of any relevant issues.
RCC_BROCHURE
Breakfast Club
Times: Monday to Friday, 7.30 am to 8.20 am Cost: £7.00 a morning Available to: children at Rockmount from full-time Reception to Year 6 Children are given the space to play, read, or do homework and are offered a healthy breakfast, including:
toast, bagels, crumpets
baked beans or scrambled egg on toast
porridge and yoghurts
After School Club
Times: Monday to Friday, 3.10pm to 6.00 pm Cost: £16.00 an evening Available to: children at Rockmount from full-time Reception to Year 6 Children take part in games, arts and crafts activities and play with their friends. A separate area is available for the younger children.
The Pabulum Menu
A "light tea" is offered to children at After School Club to keep hunger away until they get home, when they can have dinner. Healthy hot food is provided for tea, including for example:
If your child has got any allergies or dietary requirements, Pabulum will create a special menu for them. Occasionally, due to supply/delivery issues, we may need to change the menu at short notice.
Rockmount Children’s Club provides care for pupils from Reception to Year 6. Only pupils attending Rockmount Primary School will be considered for places.
Allocation will be made in order of priority. Priority is given to looked-after children and previously looked-after children, and those with siblings already in the club. Thereafter, we will allocate places on a first come, first served basis. We operate a waiting list policy for children wishing to join the club once it is full. We are unable to offer ad hoc sessions to families.
If you require a place at either the breakfast or after school club, we advise you to put in an application as soon as possible as both clubs are currently full. Your child's name can then be placed on the waiting list. Contact extendedschools@rockmount.croydon.sch.uk or telephone (020) 8683 8451 between 9:00 and 11:00am for any more information.

pageCache.text:
A Shakespearean Spectacular at Rockmount!
We were thrilled to welcome practitioners from the Globe Theatre to Rockmount for a Shakespearean Spectacular! As part of our whole school focus on Shakespeare, oracy and book-making, pupils across the school enjoyed creative and engaging workshops exploring their focus play.
Pupils from Year 1 to Year 6 took part in a lively drama workshop, each one centred around a different Shakespearean play. The children explored Shakespeare’s language with a particular focus on oracy and performance, experimenting with voice, expression, movement and character to bring the words to life. They also enjoyed a range of drama games and activities, developing their confidence, teamwork and performance skills along the way.
It was wonderful to see the children so enthusiastic and willing to get involved, showing just how much fun Shakespeare can be when you get up on your feet and perform it! A huge thank you to Jim and Susan from the Globe for leading such engaging and inspiring workshops and bringing Shakespeare to Rockmount.

Starting Reception
We warmly welcome you to Rockmount Primary School
We are pleased to share with you, lots of information about the Reception Classes at Rockmount. We hope that the following pages give you an insight into what your children will learn and achieve during their start to primary school.
Here is our Early Years brochure, where you will find information about what the Early Years Foundation Stage is, the curriculum and how to prepare your child for this exciting next step in their learning journey.
In Reception, we promote a love of learning and focus on providing an interesting and wide range of learning opportunities.
Early Years Brochure
Here are some frequently asked questions.
What do I do if my child is going to be absent from school?
Telephone the school on 020 8653 2619 and let us know the reason for your child's absence. If a child is marked absent on the morning's register, the office will follow this up.
Where do we get school uniform from?
You can find uniform information here.
Does my child need a PE kit?
Physical Development is one of the areas of learning within the EYFS curriculum and we teach aspects of it daily. We therefore do not have standalone, formalised PE lessons so your child does not need a PE kit until Year 1.
My child has allergies and dietary requirements. What do I do?
Please put this information on your enrolment form and speak to your class teacher about your child's needs.
Can I bring in snacks for my child?
Each child will be offered milk and a piece of fruit during the day, so you do not need to bring in snacks.
What happens at lunchtime?
The children will be collected by their lunchtime supervisor at 11.25am, who will then take the class to the lunch hall. The children will enjoy a balanced, healthy lunch provided by Pabulum, followed by playtime in the large playground alongside Year 1 and 2 children. (If it is raining, the children will return to their classrooms for wet play activities.) At 12.25pm, the class teacher will collect their class from the playground and return to the classroom. The lunchtime supervisor will feed back any important information to the class teacher, who will inform parents/carers at the end of the school day if necessary.
How do I pay for lunches and school trips?
Rockmount is a cashless school and we use a safe and secure payment service called Parentpay.
Is water available during the day?
Yes, water is available during the day and your child will have their own named cup.
What happens if my child has an accident at school?
Toilet accidents are inevitable as your child learns new routines. We ask that all the children bring a change of clothes with them, especially during the autumn term. Staff will assist the children to change if they need help.
Other accidents are recorded by staff. If the accident is non-urgent, the parents/carers will be informed at the end of the school day. If the accident involves the head area, you will be contacted immediately.
Will my child have homework?
Your child will have a home/school journal to draw/write about experiences that take place at home or during the weekend.
Will my child bring a reading book home?
The children are encouraged to bring books home to share with you from our reading areas. They can then change the books whenever they are ready to do so.
We teach the children to read through our phonics scheme - Read, Write Inc. There will be an opportunity for you to attend a Read, Write Inc. phonics workshop at the start of the new school year. In the meantime, please click the link above to find out more.
When can I speak to the teacher about my child's progress?
The staff are available to talk to you at the beginning and the end of each day if you have an urgent message. If you would like a longer conversation, an appointment can be made for a convenient time. We also have two Parent/Carer consultation evenings, one in the autumn term and one at the end of the spring term.
Are there clubs for my child to attend?
There are some clubs that Reception children can attend. Look at the after school activities page.
Can I use the breakfast and after school club?
Places at Rockmount Children's Club are limited. Please have a look at the RCC page to find out more.

Extra-curricular music at Rockmount:
On this page you will find choir songs (to practise at home), Musician of the Month and other music-related news and events happening in school and locally.
You may also want to explore curriculum music at Rockmount, find out how to start learning a musical instrument in school, or see and hear some of our amazing Rockmount Musicians LIVE.
Musician of the Month
In November 2023, we introduced a new whole-school musical focus: ‘Musician of the Month’. The aim is to introduce our children to a wide and diverse range of musicians, composers and musical traditions that they may not have encountered before. Each month, we explore a different musician or musical tradition, listening to their music in lessons, assemblies and in our lunch hall. Children are also encouraged to continue their musical exploration at home by researching, listening and sharing their thoughts and opinions on our Musician of the Month display board.
Over the past three years, we have explored an incredibly diverse range of music, from Mozart, Beethoven and Tchaikovsky to David Bowie, Bob Marley, Aretha Franklin and Stevie Wonder, as well as musicians and traditions from around the world, including Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, Ladysmith Black Mambazo, Gamelan Gong Kebyar and Kishori Amonkar. We have also explored the work of film composer Hans Zimmer and introduced children to lesser-known musical figures such as Florence Price, Hildegard of Bingen and Barbara Strozzi.
Through this initiative, we hope to inspire curiosity, encourage children to listen widely and help them discover music that they might otherwise never encounter. Each month, we continue to broaden our musical horizons by exploring a different musician, composer or musical tradition.
Have a listen to a YouTube playlist of all the musicians we've learnt about so far.

Musical News and Events:
There's a great article in Music Mark about the CSMA Festival concerts - an event we have proudly supported for over 10 years! You can read the article here: 850+ children. Two unforgettable nights. One incredible Festival of Music!
Congratulations to the Year 5 and 6 Choirs for performing in the CSMA Junior Concert at Fairfield Halls! The choir joined forces with several other Croydon schools to form the mass CSMA Junior Choir. For most of the choir, this was their first experience performing on stage with a live band and at such a large venue in front of an audience that had paid to see them.
Eva Smith auditioned and was selected to be one of the soloists in the song "One Little Voice." It was a magical performance, beginning with all the choirs looking down in silence so that only "one little voice" began the song. Then a second singer joined in, followed by others, until all eight singers on stage were performing together at the front. Eventually, all the children’s voices united in song.
The choir sounded amazing, and we all had a fantastic night! Well done to the choir who demonstrated an incredible amount of enthusiasm, effort, and commitment.
Year 6 Choir performs at the O2 Arena! On 22nd January, 2025 the whole of Year 6 had the incredible opportunity to take part in the Young Voices concert at the O2 Arena. Joining a mass choir of over 8,500 children, they spent the afternoon rehearsing before delivering a spectacular evening performance to a packed audience. The energy in the arena was amazing, making it a truly special event.
The event featured an exciting line up of special guests, including viral sensation MC Grammar (Jacob Mitchell), a multi-award-winning teacher-turned-rapper; Tommy Blaize, the powerhouse lead singer of the BBC Strictly Come Dancing band; and 14-year-old Souparnika Nair, who wowed audiences on Britain’s Got Talent in 2020 at just 10 years old. The children didn’t just watch the stars—they performed alongside them! In addition, they enjoyed watching spectacular performances from Urban Strides throughout the night, joining in with their high-energy dance routines, making the experience even more exciting.
A particularly moving moment of the night was when the choir performed Little Blue by Jacob Collier, a Grammy Award-winning singer, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist. The children not only sang the song but also performed it using British Sign Language (BSL), adding an extra layer of meaning and emotion to the performance. It was a truly beautiful and memorable experience for everyone involved.
Singing and dancing in such a prestigious venue, alongside professional musicians and performers, was an unforgettable experience for both the children and staff. The day was long and demanding, but the thrill of performing in such an incredible setting made every moment worthwhile.
Well done to all our amazing Rockmount Musicians for making Rockmount Proms 2024 another huge success. Photos below - to see and hear some performances from the concerts please see our Rockmount Musicians LIVE page.

For a lot of the children this was their first glimpse inside Fairfield Halls, let alone performing on the stage with a live band! The choir joined forces with several other Croydon schools to form the mass CSMA Junior Choir. The choir sounded amazing and we all (including staff!) had a fantastic night! Maximilian Dargoi auditioned and was selected to sing the solo in Nina Simone’s ‘I Wish I Knew How It Would Feel to Be Free’. Max sang amazingly well and received lots of well-deserved compliments. All the children were fantastic and demonstrated a huge amount of enthusiasm, effort and commitment.
Year 5 Choir performs at Fairfield Hall! Well done to the Year 5 Choir for performing in the CSMA Junior Concert at Fairfield Halls. For a lot of the children this was their first glimpse inside Fairfield Halls, let alone performing on the stage! The choir joined forces with several other Croydon schools to form the massive CSMA Junior Choir. The choir sounded amazing and we all (including staff!) had a fantastic night! Isobel Freeman auditioned and was selected to sing the solo in ‘Streets of London’ in the epic Singing Songbook Medley. Isobel sang amazingly well and received lots of well-deserved compliments. All the children were fantastic and demonstrated a huge amount of enthusiasm, effort and commitment.
Year 6 Choir performs at the O2 Arena! On Monday 16th January the Year 6 Choir joined together with over 9000 children to form the Young Voices Choir at the O2 Arena. We spent the afternoon rehearsing at the O2 before performing in the evening to a packed audience. The concert sounded and looked amazing!
The Young Voices Choir were joined by The Beatbox Collective and Urban strides as well as award winning singer, Heather Small! The Young Voices Choir even got to sing with Heather Small on her hit song, ‘Proud’. The performance of ‘Proud’ was recorded live on the night and is soon to be released to raise money for the charity Place2Be.
To perform at such a large venue in a choir of over 9000 children, alongside professional singers, instrumentalists, beatboxers and street dancers was a truly unforgettable experience for both the children and staff that took part. It was a lot of work and a very long and exhausting day, but totally worth it!
